questions.question: What does electric power measure?
choices: The total electrical energy transferred during use
The amount of charge passing a point alone
The rate of electrical energy transfer
The potential difference without a time rate

questions.question: Which unit measures electrical power?
choices: Watt
Coulomb
Ohm
Volt

questions.question: For a DC device, how is electric power related to voltage and current?
choices: Power equals voltage divided by time
Power equals voltage multiplied by current
Power equals current divided by voltage
Power equals resistance divided by voltage

questions.question: What does a kilowatt-hour measure?
choices: Power
Current
Resistance
Energy

questions.question: What commonly causes excessive heating in an overloaded electrical cord?
choices: Too much current through its resistance
A current below the cord's capacity in every case
A power rating lower than every connected device's rating
A decrease in the cord's resistance to exactly zero

questions.question: What does a ground-fault circuit interrupter primarily detect?
choices: The total operating time of an appliance
The temperature of the surrounding room only
A difference between outgoing and returning current
Every overcurrent, with no sensitivity to current imbalance

questions.question: What is a short circuit?
choices: A circuit operated for only a short time
An intended high-resistance path through the appliance
An unintended low-resistance path for current
A device using less power than its rated value

questions.question: Why can using several high-power devices on one circuit be a problem?
choices: Their combined current can overload the circuit
Each added device necessarily lowers total circuit current
Parallel devices divide the current so total current stays fixed
High power use has no relation to current draw

questions.question: Why should a damaged cord be taken out of use and reported to a responsible adult?
choices: Only the cord's appearance is affected
A damaged cord always supplies zero current
Insulation damage automatically lowers the electrical hazard
Exposed or damaged wiring can create shock and fire hazards

questions.question: Why are electrical appliances kept away from water during use?
choices: Water always blocks electric current completely
Water containing dissolved ions can provide a dangerous current path
Wet surroundings necessarily remove the supply voltage
Only boiling water can provide a current path

questions.question: Why does a fuse or ordinary circuit breaker not guarantee protection from every electric shock?
choices: Dangerous body current can be below the overcurrent trip level
Electric shocks always require current above the circuit's rating
Ordinary overcurrent protection measures body current directly
A breaker prevents every shock before any current can flow

questions.question: Why does a higher-power device use more energy over the same operating time?
choices: It transfers the same energy regardless of operating time
It transfers energy at a faster rate
A power rating measures only total stored energy
Higher power means a slower energy-transfer rate

questions.question: How can an appliance use less total energy despite having a higher power rating?
choices: Its power rating alone fixes energy use for every duration
It has to run for the same length of time
Voltage alone determines all energy use
It operates for a sufficiently shorter time

questions.question: Why should an appliance's grounding pin remain intact?
choices: It replaces the need for overcurrent protection
It controls only the advertised operating power
It supports the designed protective grounding connection
It stops all current during normal operation

questions.question: What is the useful distinction between power and energy on an appliance label?
choices: Power is a transfer rate; energy depends on rate and operating time
Both always measure the same quantity
Energy measures only voltage
Power measures only battery charge

questions.question: A DC device draws 2 A at 12 V. What electrical power does it use?
choices: 6 W

questions.question: A 1.2 kW heater operates for 2 hours. How much energy does it use?
choices: 0.6 kWh
2.4 kWh
1.2 kWh
3.2 kWh

questions.question: A 60 W lamp runs for 5 hours. What is its electrical energy use?
choices: 12 Wh
65 Wh
300 Wh

questions.question: Two parallel DC devices draw 3 A and 4 A from one supply. What is the total current?
choices: 1 A
7 A

questions.question: A cord is rated for less current than several appliances require together. What is the appropriate conclusion?
choices: The rating applies only to one appliance at a time
That combination can overload the cord and should not be used
Adding appliances reduces the cord's heating
The cord's insulation automatically increases its current rating
